short: A German-born cavalry commander who became the most famous Royalist general of the English Civil War and later an admiral.
full:
Prince Rupert of the Rhine was a prominent German-born soldier, admiral, and scientist, and the nephew of King Charles I. When the English Civil War broke out in 1642, the twenty-two-year-old Rupert was appointed commander of the Royalist cavalry. Known for his audacious, aggressive tactics and accompanied by his famous white poodle, Boye, he won several early victories. However, his failure to maintain discipline after breaking enemy lines frequently cost the Royalists crucial advantages, most disastrously at the Battle of Naseby in 1645.

Following the Royalist defeat and the execution of his uncle, Rupert spent years commanding a corsair fleet in exile, harassing Parliamentary shipping across Europe, Africa, and the Caribbean. After the Restoration of Charles II in 1660, he returned to England and served as a senior naval commander during the Anglo-Dutch Wars. In his later years, Rupert became a founding member of the Royal Society, conducting scientific experiments and introducing the mezzotint printmaking process to England, while also serving as the first Governor of the Hudson's Bay Company.
